pages.text: A TAG block sets the name of a value in JSON or YAML text, or hides a value from the debugging tool.

Right-click it with an empty hand. Pick the language, $(1)json$(), $(1)yaml$() or $(1)security$(), and enter the name. Tags go at the end of a struct element line or a VARIABLE or CONSTANT line. Only one tag per language fits in a line.
On a struct element, the tag replaces the element name. The name $(1)-$() skips the element. On a variable, the name is a path with dots, like $(1)server.port$().

The tag $(1)security: "sensitive"$() has only this one name, which the dialog fills in. The debugging tool shows $(1)***$() instead of the value of the variable, constant or struct element. Your program can still use the value.
Put a brown wool block in the middle and eight NOOP blocks around it. You get eight TAG blocks.
$(1)STRUCT player$(br)BEGIN$(br)  playerName STRING TAG(json: "name")$(br)END STRUCT$(br)VARIABLE port INTEGER 25565 TAG(json: "server.port")$()
